senses.gloss:
मैत्र मैत्र, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 1. मित्र), coming
or derived from a friend, given by a friend, of or
belonging to a friend; friendly, amicable, well-dis-
posed, kind, benevolent, affectionate; of or belonging
[]
to the god Mitra, q. v.; (अस्), m. ‘a friend to all
creatures,’ a Brāhman who has arrived at the highest
state of human perfection; a particular mixed caste
or degraded tribe (the offspring of an outcast
Vaiśya, Manu X. 23; cf. मैत्रेयक); scil. सन्-
धि, an alliance grounded on good-will; epithet of
the twelfth astrological Yoga; the anus, fundament;
a man's N. much used in grammatical examples [cf.
चैत्र and the Latin Caius]; N. of a preceptor;
(ई), f. (according to native authorities f. of मैत्र्य),
friendship, friendliness, good-will, (in the Buddhist
system) universal charity, love; friendship for, good-
will towards (with loc.); association, intimate con-
nection, union, contact; Benevolence personified
(daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Dharma); the
Nakṣatra Anu-rādhā; (अम्), n. friendship; the
Nakṣatra Anu-rādhā presided over by Mitra; a
prayer addressed to Mitra early in the morning;
evacuation of excrement presided over by Mitra,
(मैत्रं कृ, to discharge excrement, see Manu
IV. 152); N. of a Sūtra work; (in Ved. said to be)
= 1. मित्र, a friend.
—मैत्र-कन्यक, अस्, m. a
proper N.
—मैत्र-ता, f. friendship, friendliness,
benevolence, kindness.
—मैत्र-भ, अम्, n., N.
of the Nakṣatra Anu-rādhā.
—मैत्र-शाखा, f.,
N. of a school.
—मैत्र-सूत्र, अम्, n., N. of a
Sūtra work.
—मैत्राक्ष-ज्योतिक (˚र-अक्˚), अस्,
m., N. of a particular class of evil beings or demons
who feed on purulent carcases (Manu XII. 72).
—मैत्री-नाथ, अस्, m., N. of an author.
—मैत्री-
पूर्व, अस्, आ, अम्, preceded by friendship.
—मैत्री-
बल, अस्, आ, अम्, whose strength is benevolence;
(अस्), m. epithet of a Buddha; N. of a king (re-
garded as an incarnation of Śākya-muni).
—मैत्री-
भाव, अस्, m. state of friendliness, friendship.

मैत्रवर्धक (fr. मित्र-वर्ध; also read
मैत्रवर्ध्रक, fr. मित्र-वर्ध्र), see Gaṇa
Dhūmādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 127.

मैत्राबार्हस्पत्य, Ved. belonging or pertain-
ing to Mitra and Bṛhas-pati.

मैत्रायण, अम्, n. (fr. मैत्र + अयन), be-
nevolence; (अस्), m. a patronymic, see Gaṇa Naḍādi
to Pāṇ. IV. 1. 89, (in this sense fr. 1. मित्र); N.
of the author of a Gṛhya-sūtra; (आस्), m. pl., N. of
a school (named after Maitri); (ई), f., N. of the
mother of Pūrṇa; of a female teacher.
—मैत्रा-
यण-गृह्य-पद्धति, इस्, f., N. of a work by
Prathama-puruṣa on the sixteen Saṃskāras.

मैत्रायणक, see Gaṇa Arīhaṇāid to Pāṇ. IV.
2, 80.
मैत्रायणि or मैत्रायणी, N. of an Upaniṣad.

मैत्रायणीय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a school.
—मै-
त्रायणीय-परिशिष्ट, अम्, n., N. of a work.

मैत्रावरुण, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. descended or
derived from Mitra and Varuṇa, of or belonging to
them; (अस्), m. a patronymic (see Ṛg-veda VII.
33, 11); of Agastya; of Vālmīki; epithet of one of
the officiating priests (the first assistant of the Hotṛ,
who was also called Pra-śāstṛ; cf. कोकिल-म्˚).
—मैत्रावरुण-श्रुति, इस्, f., N. of a work.

मैत्रावरुणि, इस्, m. the son of Mitra and
Varuṇa, a patronymic of Mānya or Agastya; of
Vasiṣṭha; of Vālmīki.

मैत्रावरुणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. relating to
the Maitrāvaruṇa Ṛtvij; (अम्), n. the office of the
preceding.

मैत्रि, इस्, m., Ved., N. of a teacher (from whom
the Maitry-upaniṣad derives its title).

मैत्रिक, अम्, n. (fr. 1. मित्र or मैत्र), a
friendly office, (used at the end of an adj. comp.)

मैत्रिन्, ई, इणी, इ (fr. मैत्र), friendly, benevo-
lent, a friend.

मैत्रेय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. मैत्री), friendly, re-
lating to a friend, benevolent; (अस्), m. (fr. मि-
त्रयु), a patronymic of Kauṣārava; of Glāva,
(according to a Scholiast a metronymic fr. मित्रा);
N. of a Bodhi-sattva and future Buddha; of the
Vidūṣaka in the Mṛc-chakaṭikā; of a grammarian
(= मैत्रेय-रक्षित); a particular mixed caste,
[]
= मैत्रेयक; (ई), f., N. of an Upaniṣad (pro-
bably as composed by Maitri); of the wife of Yājña-
valkya; of certain other women.
—मैत्रेय-रक्-
षित, अस्, m., N. of a grammarian.
—मैत्रेय-
वन, अम्, n., N. of a forest.
—मैत्रेय-सूत्र,
अम्, n., N. of a Sūtra work.

मैत्रेयक, अस्, m., N. of a particular mixed
caste or degraded tribe (the offspring of a Vaideha
father by an Ayogavī, whose business is to praise
great men and announce the dawn by ringing a bell,
Manu X. 33); (इका), f. descent from Mitrayu;
a contest between friends or allies (= मित्र-युद्-
ध).
